Algebra I · Lesson 5.6

Three or More Variables

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Some stories name three quantities and state three facts, so the system has three letters and three equations. No new method is needed for that. One substitution, or one elimination, takes the count from three letters down to two, and 5.2 and 5.3 already solve what is left. The next two problems run that once, on one system.

Problem
The system x=4z+7x=4z+7, 2x+3y+5z=2552x+3y+5z=255, and 3x+y−2z=1753x+y−2z=175 has three letters, and the first equation is already solved for xx. Write 4z+74z+7 in place of xx in both of the other two, which leaves two equations in yy and zz alone. Solve that pair and enter zz.
Show a hint
  • One equation is already solved for a letter, so 4z+74z+7 can stand wherever xx stands. Do the replacement in the second equation and in the third, not in just one of them.
  • After the replacement the second equation collects to 3y+13z=2413y+13z=241 and the third to y+10z=154y+10z=154. In y+10z=154y+10z=154, yy has coefficient 11.
Show the full solution
Substituting x=4z+7x=4z+7 gives 2(4z+7)+3y+5z=2552(4z+7)+3y+5z=255, which collects to 3y+13z=2413y+13z=241, and 3(4z+7)+y−2z=1753(4z+7)+y−2z=175, which collects to y+10z=154y+10z=154. From y+10z=154y+10z=154, y=154−10zy=154−10z, so 3(154−10z)+13z=2413(154−10z)+13z=241, then 462−17z=241462−17z=241 and 17z=22117z=221, so z=13z=13​. Both replacements are needed, since doing only one leaves an equation that still carries xx rather than a pair in yy and zz.
Problem
Same system as the last problem, and z=13z=13 is now known. Find yy and xx, then check the triple in all three original equations and enter x+yx+y.
Show a hint
  • One of the two reduced equations is y+10z=154y+10z=154, and with zz known only yy is left in it.
  • Neither reduced equation has an xx in it, so xx comes only from x=4z+7x=4z+7, the equation that was already solved for it.
Show the full solution
y+10(13)=154y+10(13)=154 gives y=24y=24, and x=4(13)+7=59x=4(13)+7=59, so x+y=83x+y=83​. The triple (59,24,13)(59,24,13) passes all three originals, 59=4(13)+759=4(13)+7, 118+72+65=255118+72+65=255, and 177+24−26=175177+24−26=175. Two back-substitutions are needed, one for the second letter of the reduced pair and one for the letter that was replaced.
Key idea
One substitution, one fewer letter. Solve one equation for one letter and write that expression in place of the letter in both of the other two equations. That removes the letter from both at once, and what is left is two equations in two letters, which 5.2 and 5.3 solve. Substituting into only one of them leaves two equations still carrying three letters, and two facts cannot pin three quantities. Back-substitution then runs twice, once into the reduced pair for its second letter and once into the equation that was solved, since that letter never appeared in the reduced pair.
Problem
In 3x+4y+2z=1503x+4y+2z=150 5x+2y−2z=1085x+2y−2z=108 4x+3y+6z=2314x+3y+6z=231 no letter has coefficient 11 anywhere, so isolating one starts with a division. The zz-terms are the cheap ones to match. Eliminate zz, once from the first and second equations and once from the first and third. Solve the two-letter system that comes out and enter xx.
Show a hint
  • The zz-terms are +2z+2z, −2z−2z and +6z+6z. The first two are opposite already, and tripling the first equation matches the 6z6z in the third.
  • Adding the first two equations leaves 8x+6y=2588x+6y=258, and three times the first minus the third leaves 5x+9y=2195x+9y=219. Every term of 8x+6y=2588x+6y=258 divides by 22.
Show the full solution
Adding the first two equations clears zz and gives 8x+6y=2588x+6y=258, or 4x+3y=1294x+3y=129. Three times the first equation minus the third gives 5x+9y=2195x+9y=219. Tripling 4x+3y=1294x+3y=129 gives 12x+9y=38712x+9y=387, and subtracting leaves 7x=1687x=168, so x=24x=24​. Then 3y=129−96=333y=129−96=33 gives y=11y=11, and 2z=150−72−44=342z=150−72−44=34 gives z=17z=17. Check in the third equation, 96+33+102=23196+33+102=231.
Problem
Here is a system in three letters. 5x+2y+3z=1615x+2y+3z=161 4x−2y+5z=554x−2y+5z=55 3x+4y−2z=1383x+4y−2z=138 Clear yy from two different pairs of equations, solve the two-letter system that is left, and enter yy.
Show a hint
  • The yy-terms are +2y+2y, −2y−2y and +4y+4y. The first two are opposite already, and doubling the second equation makes −4y−4y, the opposite of the third's +4y+4y.
  • With those pairings the reduced pair is 9x+8z=2169x+8z=216 and 11x+8z=24811x+8z=248, both carrying 8z8z, so subtracting leaves xx alone. The ask is yy, which appears in neither.
Show the full solution
Adding the first two equations gives 9x+8z=2169x+8z=216. Adding twice the second equation to the third gives 11x+8z=24811x+8z=248. Subtracting leaves 2x=322x=32, so x=16x=16, then 8z=216−144=728z=216−144=72 and z=9z=9. Back in the first equation, 2y=161−80−27=542y=161−80−27=54, so y=27y=27​. Check, 4(16)−2(27)+5(9)=554(16)−2(27)+5(9)=55 and 3(16)+4(27)−2(9)=1383(16)+4(27)−2(9)=138. The letter cleared first is not in the reduced pair, so an original equation is the only place left to find its value.
Key idea
Clear one letter from two different pairs. Pick one letter, eliminate it from one pair of the three equations and then from a different pair, and what is left is two equations in the other two letters. Combining the same pair a second way only rescales the equation already found, so the second line is a copy of the first and two letters are left with one fact between them. Which letter to clear is 5.3's cheapness question, asked across three coefficients instead of two. Check the finished triple in all three original equations, since a triple built from two of them need not fit the third.
Problem
In 4x+3y+5z=2734x+3y+5z=273 7x+6y+8z=4717x+6y+8z=471 5x+9y−6z=775x+9y−6z=77 one letter is cheaper to eliminate than the other two. Clear that letter from two different pairs of these equations, solve the two-letter system that is left, and enter zz.
Show a hint
  • 5.3 clears the letter whose coefficients meet at the smaller multiple. The two yy-pairs used here meet at 66 and 99, while the cheapest xx-pair meets at 2020 and the cheapest zz-pair at 2424.
  • Doubling the first equation makes its yy term 6y6y, matching the second, and subtracting leaves x+2z=75x+2z=75. Tripling the first makes that term 9y9y, matching the third, which gives a second equation in xx and zz.
Show the full solution
Doubling the first equation and subtracting the second gives x+2z=75x+2z=75. Tripling the first and subtracting the third gives 7x+21z=7427x+21z=742, which divides by 77 to x+3z=106x+3z=106. Subtracting those two leaves z=31z=31​. Back-substituting gives x=13x=13 and y=22y=22, and (13,22,31)(13,22,31) checks in all three originals. Clearing xx instead would take 28x28x in one pair and 20x20x in the other, with right sides up to 19111911 instead of 819819.

A question does not have to ask for a letter. It can ask for x+y+zx+y+z, or for the cost of one of each item. At a solution all three equations are true, so adding them adds equal numbers to equal numbers, and the result is one more true statement about that triple. Sometimes its left side is exactly the quantity the question named.

Problem
These three equations hold at once for the same xx, yy, and zz. 5x+2y+7z=2385x+2y+7z=238 4x+6y+3z=2644x+6y+3z=264 3x+4y+2z=1823x+4y+2z=182 Add all three, left side to left side and right side to right side, then enter x+y+zx+y+z without solving for the letters one at a time.
Show a hint
  • Look at the three coefficients in each letter's column. The xx-column, the yy-column, and the zz-column all come to the same number here.
  • Adding the three equations gives 12x+12y+12z=68412x+12y+12z=684, and each term there is a multiple of 1212.
Show the full solution
Adding the three left sides gives 12x+12y+12z12x+12y+12z, and adding the three right sides gives 684684, so 12(x+y+z)=68412(x+y+z)=684 and x+y+z=57x+y+z=57​. The triple is (18,25,14)(18,25,14), but reaching it takes two rounds of elimination and two back-substitutions, while one addition and one division give the sum.
Key idea
Build the quantity that was asked for. Any sum, difference or multiple of the three equations is true at the solution, which is 5.3's rule with a third equation added. When the question asks for a combination, look for a combination of the three that produces it before solving anything. Adding all three works whenever each letter's coefficients add to the same number, since the sum is then that number times x+y+zx+y+z, and dividing by it gives the answer. Solving in full is never wrong, only longer, and the separate letters can be fractions even when the combination is a whole number.
Problem
7x+3y+5z=2077x+3y+5z=207 4x+8y+2z=1964x+8y+2z=196 5x+5y+z=1455x+5y+z=145 The ask is x+y+zx+y+z and not any one letter. No letter in this system has a whole-number value, so a full solve ends in fractions for all three. Find a combination of the three equations whose left side is a multiple of x+y+zx+y+z, then enter x+y+zx+y+z.
Show a hint
  • Add the columns of all three equations first. They come to 1616, 1616 and 88, so a plain sum is not a multiple of x+y+zx+y+z. A minus sign on one of the three is the next thing to try.
  • The first plus the second minus the third leaves 66 in every column.
Show the full solution
Adding the first two equations and subtracting the third gives (7+4−5)x+(3+8−5)y+(5+2−1)z=207+196−145(7+4−5)x+(3+8−5)y+(5+2−1)z=207+196−145, which is 6x+6y+6z=2586x+6y+6z=258, so x+y+z=43x+y+z=43​. The triple itself is (434,594,352)(443​,459​,235​), so a full solve ends in quarters for all three letters, while the combination takes one line.
Fun fact
In 1801 the new asteroid Ceres was lost in the sun's glare. Carl Friedrich Gauss, then 24, turned six weeks of sightings into equations, solved them, and said where to look. Telescopes found it that December.

This is 5.5's routine with the count raised again. Name all three quantities with units, write one equation for each stated fact, solve, then read the problem's last sentence again to see which quantity it asked for. A triangle's three angles are one such story, since the angle sum is a stated fact like any other.

Problem
A framing shop charges one fixed price to cut a mat, one to fit glass, and one to assemble a frame. One job of 3 mats cut, 2 sheets of glass fitted and 1 frame assembled came to 129 dollars. A second job of 2 mats, 4 glass sheets and 3 frames came to 237 dollars. A third of 5 mats, 1 glass sheet and 2 frames came to 166 dollars. Enter the price of fitting one sheet of glass, in dollars.
Show a hint
  • Three prices are unknown, so name all three with units and write one equation per job.
  • With mm, gg and ff the three prices in dollars, 3m+2g+f=1293m+2g+f=129, 2m+4g+3f=2372m+4g+3f=237 and 5m+g+2f=1665m+g+2f=166. The ff-column is 11, 33, 22, so scaling the first job and subtracting clears ff against either of the other two.
Show the full solution
With mm, gg and ff the three prices in dollars, 3m+2g+f=1293m+2g+f=129, 2m+4g+3f=2372m+4g+3f=237 and 5m+g+2f=1665m+g+2f=166. Three times the first minus the second gives 7m+2g=1507m+2g=150, and twice the first minus the third gives m+3g=92m+3g=92. Then m=92−3gm=92−3g, so 7(92−3g)+2g=1507(92−3g)+2g=150, giving 644−19g=150644−19g=150 and g=26g=26​. Then m=14m=14 and f=35f=35, and the second job checks, 28+104+105=23728+104+105=237.
Problem
A tea seller charges one fixed price per tin of green tea, one per tin of black tea and one per tin of herbal tea. One order of 4 green, 1 black and 3 herbal tins cost 59 dollars. A second order of 3 green, 5 black and 2 herbal cost 89 dollars. A third order of 2 green, 3 black and 4 herbal cost 77 dollars. Enter the combined cost of one tin of each, in dollars.
Show a hint
  • Name the three tin prices with units and write one equation per order. The ask is the three prices added together, not any one of them, so look for a combination of the three equations that lands on that sum.
  • Add the three green coefficients, then the three black coefficients, then the three herbal coefficients. Each of those totals is 99, so adding the three equations gives nine of every price at once.
Show the full solution
With gg, bb and hh the green, black and herbal tin prices in dollars, 4g+b+3h=594g+b+3h=59, 3g+5b+2h=893g+5b+2h=89 and 2g+3b+4h=772g+3b+4h=77. The three green coefficients add to 99, and so do the black and the herbal, so adding the three equations gives 9g+9b+9h=2259g+9b+9h=225 and g+b+h=25g+b+h=25​. Solving the whole system gives 66, 1111 and 88 dollars, which is more work than this ask needs.

4x+9=254x+9=25 is true for one value of xx and false for every other. 2(x+3)=2x+62(x+3)=2x+6 is true for every value. The second is a stronger claim, and with unknown constants in it the claim is about them, not about xx. A claim that holds at every xx holds at whichever values are easiest to substitute, and each gives an equation in the constants.

Problem
a(x+6)+b(x−4)=17x+22a(x+6)+b(x−4)=17x+22 is true for every value of xx. Substitute x=0x=0, then substitute x=1x=1. Each substitution gives one equation in aa and bb. Solve that system and enter aa.
Show a hint
  • The statement holds at every xx, so it holds at x=0x=0 and at x=1x=1, and each of those is an ordinary equation in aa and bb.
  • At x=0x=0 the statement reads 6a−4b=226a−4b=22. At x=1x=1 it reads 7a−3b=397a−3b=39. That pair is 5.3's territory, and the bb-coefficients −4−4 and −3−3 both divide −12−12.
Show the full solution
At x=0x=0, 6a−4b=226a−4b=22. At x=1x=1, 7a−3b=397a−3b=39. Tripling the first and quadrupling the second gives 18a−12b=6618a−12b=66 and 28a−12b=15628a−12b=156, and subtracting leaves 10a=9010a=90, so a=9a=9​. Then b=8b=8, and a check at x=2x=2 gives, 9(8)+8(−2)=569(8)+8(−2)=56 and 17(2)+22=5617(2)+22=56. The same aa and bb come out whatever two values of xx are used, and substituting x=4x=4 or x=−6x=−6 makes one term zero, which pins one letter in a single line.
Key idea
Matching coefficients. If Ax+B=Cx+DAx+B=Cx+D is true for every value of xx, then A=CA=C and B=DB=D. Subtracting Cx+DCx+D from both sides gives (A−C)x=D−B(A−C)x=D−B. With A−CA−C not zero, that is a one-letter equation of the kind chapter 4 solves, so it is true at exactly one value of xx and false at every other, which is not what was assumed. So A−C=0A−C=0, and then D−B=0D−B=0 as well. Matching the xx column and then the constants gives the same system that substituting two values of xx gives, with none of the arithmetic.
Problem
a(x+2y+1)+b(3x−y+2)+c(x+y+4)=106x+19y+113a(x+2y+1)+b(3x−y+2)+c(x+y+4)=106x+19y+113 is true for every value of xx and every value of yy. Collect the left side, match the xx column, the yy column and the constants, then solve the three equations in aa, bb and cc. Enter aa.
Show a hint
  • Collect the whole left side into an xx-part, a yy-part and a constant part before comparing anything. The xx-part is (a+3b+c)x(a+3b+c)x.
  • The three matches are a+3b+c=106a+3b+c=106, 2a−b+c=192a−b+c=19 and a+2b+4c=113a+2b+4c=113. The first two carry the same cc-coefficient, so subtracting one from the other clears cc with no scaling.
Show the full solution
Collecting gives (a+3b+c)x+(2a−b+c)y+(a+2b+4c)(a+3b+c)x+(2a−b+c)y+(a+2b+4c), so a+3b+c=106a+3b+c=106, 2a−b+c=192a−b+c=19 and a+2b+4c=113a+2b+4c=113. Subtracting the second from the first clears cc and gives −a+4b=87−a+4b=87. Subtracting the third from four times the first also clears cc and gives 3a+10b=3113a+10b=311. From a=4b−87a=4b−87, 12b−261+10b=31112b−261+10b=311, so 22b=57222b=572 and b=26b=26, which gives a=17a=17​. Then c=11c=11. A statement true for every xx and every yy gives one match per column, three in all, which is exactly the number of equations needed to find aa, bb and cc.

5.1's three counts carry over. Three equations in three letters usually pin one triple, and it fails in the two ways 5.3 named. Combining them down to a false statement like 0=70=7 means no triple fits all three. Reaching 0=00=0 means one of the three follows from the other two, leaving two facts for three letters and infinitely many triples.

Problem
For exactly one value of kk, the system 4x+3y+2z=1584x+3y+2z=158, 5x−y+6z=1435x−y+6z=143, 9x+2y+8z=k9x+2y+8z=k has infinitely many solutions, and for every other value it has none. Enter that kk.
Show a hint
  • Compare the third equation's left side with the sum of the first two left sides, column by column.
  • The first two left sides add to exactly the third left side, so for any triple satisfying the first two equations the value of 9x+2y+8z9x+2y+8z is already known. Match kk to it.
Show the full solution
Adding the first two equations gives 9x+2y+8z=3019x+2y+8z=301, which is the third equation exactly when k=301k=301​. At that kk only two of the three equations are independent, and two equations in three letters have infinitely many solutions. At any other kk, subtracting the first two equations from the third leaves 0=k−3010=k−301, which is false, so no triple works.
Key idea
What carried over. No method here is new. Substitution and elimination each remove one letter, so a system in three letters becomes one in two, and chapter 4 solves the one-letter equation at the end. Back-substitution then recovers the letters in reverse order, one step per letter removed. The three counts from 5.1 and the two leftover statements mean what they did with two letters. With four letters and four facts, one more round of the same step is all that changes. What is new is the check, since a triple has to satisfy all three original equations and not only the two it came from.

That closes chapter 5. A system is a set of facts about the same letters, and every method in the chapter removed letters one at a time until a single value was left, whatever the count started at. Chapter 6, Ratios, Percents and Proportion, opens with 6.1 Ratios, Simple and Subtle.

Practice these ideas

Practice
In 5x+2y+3z=2815x+2y+3z=281, two of the three letters are already known, x=23x=23 and y=41y=41. Enter zz.
Show the solution
Substituting gives 115+82+3z=281115+82+3z=281, so 3z=281−197=843z=281−197=84 and z=28z=28​. Check, 115+82+84=281115+82+84=281.
Practice
Of y=2z+5y=2z+5, 3x+y+4z=1493x+y+4z=149 and x+2y+3z=128x+2y+3z=128, the first is already solved for yy. Substitute that expression into the other two, solve the pair in xx and zz that is left, and enter xx.
Show the solution
Substituting gives 3x+(2z+5)+4z=1493x+(2z+5)+4z=149, which collects to 3x+6z=1443x+6z=144, or x+2z=48x+2z=48, and x+2(2z+5)+3z=128x+2(2z+5)+3z=128, which collects to x+7z=118x+7z=118. Subtracting leaves 5z=705z=70, so z=14z=14 and x=48−2(14)=20x=48−2(14)=20​. Then y=2(14)+5=33y=2(14)+5=33. Check, 3(20)+33+4(14)=1493(20)+33+4(14)=149 and 20+2(33)+3(14)=12820+2(33)+3(14)=128.
Practice
A student reports (x,y,z)=(15,9,22)(x,y,z)=(15,9,22) as the solution of 2x+3y+z=792x+3y+z=79, 4x+y+2z=1134x+y+2z=113 and 3x+5y+4z=1883x+5y+4z=188. Enter how many of the three equations the triple satisfies.
Show the solution
The triple gives 30+27+22=7930+27+22=79, then 60+9+44=11360+9+44=113, then 45+45+88=17845+45+88=178, which misses 188188, so the triple satisfies 22​ of the three. The true solution is (13,9,26)(13,9,26). A triple built from two of the equations satisfies those two automatically, so it is whichever equation was left out that does the checking.
Practice
Clear zz from two different pairs of 2x+3y+3z=1802x+3y+3z=180, 4x+2y−3z=264x+2y−3z=26 and 5x−3y+3z=1475x−3y+3z=147, solve the two-letter system that comes out, and enter yy.
Show the solution
Adding the first two equations gives 6x+5y=2066x+5y=206, and adding the second to the third gives 9x−y=1739x−y=173. From y=9x−173y=9x−173, 6x+5(9x−173)=2066x+5(9x−173)=206, so 51x=107151x=1071 and x=21x=21, then y=189−173=16y=189−173=16​, and 3z=180−42−48=903z=180−42−48=90 gives z=30z=30. Check in the third equation, 105−48+90=147105−48+90=147.
Practice
In 6x+5y+7z=3126x+5y+7z=312, 6x+8y+4z=3486x+8y+4z=348 and 6x+4y+9z=3156x+4y+9z=315, one letter has the same coefficient in all three equations. Clear that letter from two different pairs, then enter the value of that same letter.
Show the solution
Subtracting the first equation from the second gives 3y−3z=363y−3z=36, so y−z=12y−z=12, and subtracting the third from the first gives y−2z=−3y−2z=−3. Subtracting those two leaves z=15z=15, then y=27y=27, and 6x=312−135−105=726x=312−135−105=72, so x=12x=12​. Check in the second equation, 72+216+60=34872+216+60=348. The reduced pair has no xx in it, so xx is found last, by substituting yy and zz into an original equation.
Practice
In 5x+2y+z=1515x+2y+z=151, 2x+5y+z=1722x+5y+z=172 and x+y+6z=109x+y+6z=109, enter x+y+zx+y+z.
Show the solution
Adding the three equations gives 8x+8y+8z=4328x+8y+8z=432, so x+y+z=54x+y+z=54​. The triple is (18,25,11)(18,25,11), which the question never needed. Adding works here because each letter's three coefficients total the same number.
Practice
One triple (x,y,z)(x,y,z) satisfies all three of 8x+5y+6z=3878x+5y+6z=387, 8x+2y+3z=2348x+2y+3z=234 and 5x+7y−4z=2075x+7y−4z=207. Enter y+zy+z for that triple.
Show the solution
Subtracting the second equation from the first gives 3y+3z=1533y+3z=153, and dividing by 3 gives y+z=51y+z=51​. The full triple is (14,31,20)(14,31,20), but one subtraction is enough for y+zy+z, with no use for the third equation.
Practice
The three angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees. The second angle is 21 degrees more than the first, and the first two together are 30 degrees more than the third. Enter the largest of the three angles, in degrees.
Show the solution
With aa, bb and cc the three angles in degrees, a+b+c=180a+b+c=180, b=a+21b=a+21 and a+b=c+30a+b=c+30. Substituting the third into the first gives (c+30)+c=180(c+30)+c=180, so c=75c=75 and a+b=105a+b=105. With b=a+21b=a+21, 2a+21=1052a+21=105 gives a=42a=42 and b=63b=63, so the largest angle is 7575​ degrees. Check, 42+63+75=18042+63+75=180. The ask is the largest angle, not the letter solved for first.
Practice
A depot stacks three sizes of box, each size the same mass. One pallet of 2 small, 3 medium and 1 large box weighs 74 kg. A second of 1 small, 2 medium and 3 large weighs 94 kg. A third of 4 small, 1 medium and 2 large weighs 103 kg. Enter the mass of one large box, in kilograms.
Show the solution
With ss, mm and ll the three masses in kilograms, 2s+3m+l=742s+3m+l=74, s+2m+3l=94s+2m+3l=94 and 4s+m+2l=1034s+m+2l=103. Twice the second minus the first gives m+5l=114m+5l=114, and four times the second minus the third gives 7m+10l=2737m+10l=273. Then m=114−5lm=114−5l, so 798−35l+10l=273798−35l+10l=273, giving 25l=52525l=525 and l=21l=21​. Then m=9m=9 and s=13s=13, and the third pallet checks, 52+9+42=10352+9+42=103.
Practice
Constants aa and bb make a(x−5)+b(x+3)=24x−8a(x−5)+b(x+3)=24x−8 true for every value of xx. Enter bb.
Show the solution
At x=5x=5 the aa-term is zero, so 8b=24(5)−8=1128b=24(5)−8=112 and b=14b=14​. At x=−3x=−3 the bb-term is zero and −8a=−80−8a=−80 gives a=10a=10. Matching coefficients instead gives a+b=24a+b=24 and −5a+3b=−8−5a+3b=−8, which the same pair satisfies.
Practice
Constants aa and bb make (3a+b)x+(a−2b)=63x+7(3a+b)x+(a−2b)=63x+7 true for every value of xx, not for one value only. Enter aa.
Show the solution
Matching the xx-parts and the constants gives 3a+b=633a+b=63 and a−2b=7a−2b=7. Doubling the first gives 6a+2b=1266a+2b=126, and adding a−2b=7a−2b=7 leaves 7a=1337a=133, so a=19a=19​, with b=6b=6. Check, 3(19)+6=633(19)+6=63 and 19−2(6)=719−2(6)=7.
Practice
The system 3x+4y−2z=913x+4y−2z=91, 5x−y+3z=625x−y+3z=62 and 8x+3y+z=1608x+3y+z=160 has three equations in three letters, which is usually enough to pin down one triple. Enter the number of solutions this system has.
Show the solution
Adding the first two equations gives 8x+3y+z=1538x+3y+z=153, the same left side as the third but with 153153 on the right in place of 160160. Subtracting leaves 0=70=7, false at every triple, so the count is 00​. The first two equations on their own have plenty of solutions, so a triple has to pass all three before it counts.
Practice
The system x+y+z=96x+y+z=96, 2x−y+3z=2172x−y+3z=217, 4x+y+5z=4094x+y+5z=409 has a third equation that follows from the first two, so there are infinitely many solutions. Exactly one of them has y=0y=0. Enter xx for that one.
Show the solution
With y=0y=0, the first two equations read x+z=96x+z=96 and 2x+3z=2172x+3z=217. Substituting x=96−zx=96−z gives 192+z=217192+z=217, so z=25z=25 and x=71x=71​. Check all three, 71+0+25=9671+0+25=96, then 142−0+75=217142−0+75=217, then 284+0+125=409284+0+125=409. Twice the first equation plus the second gives the third, which is why the system leaves one letter free.
Practice
Only two facts are known about three letters, 5x+2y+3z=2145x+2y+3z=214 and x+4y+3z=152x+4y+3z=152, so no one letter has a single value here. Enter x+y+zx+y+z.
Show the solution
Adding the two equations gives 6x+6y+6z=3666x+6y+6z=366, so x+y+z=61x+y+z=61​. No single letter is available here, since xx, yy and zz each take infinitely many values across the solutions, while their sum takes only this one.
Practice
Solve 2(x+y)−z=492(x+y)−z=49, 3x−(y−2z)=863x−(y−2z)=86 and x+4(y+z)=179x+4(y+z)=179. Clear one letter to leave two equations in the other two, finish from there, and enter zz.
Show the solution
Cleaning gives 2x+2y−z=492x+2y−z=49, 3x−y+2z=863x−y+2z=86 and x+4y+4z=179x+4y+4z=179. Twice the second plus the first gives 8x+3z=2218x+3z=221, and four times the second plus the third gives 13x+12z=52313x+12z=523. Multiplying 8x+3z=2218x+3z=221 by 44 gives 32x+12z=88432x+12z=884, and subtracting 13x+12z=52313x+12z=523 leaves 19x=36119x=361, so x=19x=19. Then 3z=221−152=693z=221−152=69 gives z=23z=23​, with y=17y=17. Check the second original, 57−(17−46)=57+29=8657−(17−46)=57+29=86. The minus in front of the bracket reaches both terms inside.
Practice
A supplier charges fixed unit prices for valves, gaskets and couplings. One shipment of 6 valves, 2 gaskets and 3 couplings cost 111 dollars. A second shipment of 2 valves, 7 gaskets and 4 couplings cost 158 dollars. A third shipment of 3 valves, 4 gaskets and 2 couplings cost 99 dollars. Enter the cost of one valve, one gasket and one coupling together, in dollars.
Show the solution
With vv, gg and cc the three unit prices in dollars, 6v+2g+3c=1116v+2g+3c=111, 2v+7g+4c=1582v+7g+4c=158 and 3v+4g+2c=993v+4g+2c=99. The first plus the second minus the third gives 5v+5g+5c=111+158−99=1705v+5g+5c=111+158−99=170, so v+g+c=34v+g+c=34​. The separate prices are 77, 1212 and 1515, and solving for all three takes two eliminations and two back-substitutions while the combination takes one line.
Practice
Solve the four-letter system 4w+x+y+z=1324w+x+y+z=132, w+4x+y+z=168w+4x+y+z=168, w+x+4y+z=114w+x+4y+z=114 and w+x+y+4z=153w+x+y+4z=153. Enter xx, not the whole solution.
Show the solution
Adding all four equations gives 7(w+x+y+z)=5677(w+x+y+z)=567, so w+x+y+z=81w+x+y+z=81. The second equation is 3x+(w+x+y+z)=1683x+(w+x+y+z)=168, so 3x=873x=87 and x=29x=29​. The full solution is (17,29,11,24)(17,29,11,24). Clearing one letter at a time reaches the same answer in three rounds of elimination, while the total gets there in two lines.
